results.title: For many taxa, museum specimens can help fill in research holes - The Wildlife Society
results.content: + From Consultation to Collaboration: Centering Tribal Voices in Conservation Webinar on: on October 29, 2025 4:00 pm + TWS Legacy Giving: Retirement Giving for Wildlife Conservation Webinar on: on November 19, 2025 12:00 pm ### Share this article # For many taxa, museum specimens can help fill in research holes September 21, 2021 by **Dana Kobilinsky** In 2019, researchers had been looking at the abundance of native and non-native ant species in Florida. Examining a museum dataset spanning 60 years of collections, they found that non-native species were becoming relatively more abundant. But just because there were records of non-native species in museum collections, did that mean they were also more abundant in the wild? Worried about getting a skeptical reviewer, the researchers wanted to make sure museum records really reflected the abundance of wildlife and plants in the field. In a study published in *Methods in Ecology and Evolution*, the researchers reached out to a number of museums to compare their collections to field studies and determine how abundance matched up. I thought, let’s go ahead and compare those records to standardized survey data collected by field ecologists.” Gotelli and his co-authors began contacting museum specialists and taxonomic experts and assembled 17 high-quality datasets of museum records and field data from roughly the same time period and place. As with the Florida ant data, species that were common in the field were represented by many museum records, and species that were rare in the field were represented by few museum records. They want the rare things and to fill out their collection with species they don’t already have.” As a result, Gotelli said, researchers need to be careful using museum records to gauge abundance. Nevertheless, the consistent signal in museum and field collections means that researchers can use the museum records to understand trends in relative abundance. In places without adequate field surveys, researchers can determine which species are relatively common and which are relatively rare by looking at their frequencies in museum collections. While the research shows some of the limitations of museum collections, for Gotelli, it also shows the opportunities they present when field research is out of the question.

results.content: Automated annotation of rare-cell types from single-cell RNA-sequencing data through synthetic oversampling | bioRxiv. The second use case was designed to jointly use snRNA-Seq data and scRNA-Seq on a lower imbalance ratio (∼1 to 26) for the training step to likewise investigate the potential of the algorithm to consider both single cell capture procedures and the impact of “less” rare-cell types. Here, we show how the limitation of identifying already annotated rare-cell types in newly generated scRNA-Seq data can be overcome, by using an synthetic oversampling approach (sc-SynO). Machine learning (ML) algorithms are widely used to deal with classification problems and, thus, are used here to automate the annotation of rare-cell types from single-cell or nuclei RNA-Seq data. * **sc-SynO:** Our proposed approach is based on the LoRAS algorithm and integrates the idea of approximating the minority class data manifold with a more comprehensive modelling of the convex data space of the minority class, while generating synthetic minority class samples resulting in more balanced model performance in terms of F1-Score and Balanced accuracy [11]. To evaluate the potential of synthetic oversampling to precisely annotate cell populations in newly generated data, we generated two use cases by utilizing already published single-cell and nuclei RNA-Seq datasets. In contrast to this, the second use case was designed to jointly use snRNA-Seq data and scRNA-Seq on a lower imbalance ratio (∼1 to 26) for the training step to likewise investigate the potential of the algorithm to consider both single cell capture procedures and the impact of “less” rare-cell types. **c)** Based on the data input, we utilize the LoRAS synthetic oversampling algorithms to generate new cells around the former origin of cells to increase the size of the minority sample. For the Glial cell dataset, with only 17 minority class samples, we use three of the nearest neighbours of a minority class sample, as well as the oversampling neighbourhood of all algorithms. Applying sc-SynO on a novel dataset to identify the same rare-cell type is magnitudes less time-consuming than manually curated data processing and annotation of scRNA-Seq data. 3. results.title: How Can Data Augmentation Reduce Bias? → Question
results.content: In the context of sustainability, where datasets can be limited or biased, data augmentation can be a very useful tool. The importance of data augmentation in addressing bias stems from its ability to create a more representative dataset. > Data augmentation helps create a more balanced dataset by generating variations of existing data, addressing bias by ensuring all groups are better represented. By applying these techniques, data augmentation can help create a more diverse and representative dataset, leading to models that are less biased and more effective in real-world applications. The power of data augmentation in reducing bias lies in its ability to address the inherent imbalances present in many real-world datasets. Data augmentation can help to correct this by generating synthetic data that increases the representation of these underrepresented groups, thereby promoting more equitable model performance. Data augmentation can help to bridge this gap by generating synthetic data that reflects the experiences of these underrepresented communities, leading to more effective and equitable solutions. Data augmentation can help to address this by generating synthetic data for endangered species, increasing their representation in the training data. > Data augmentation corrects data imbalances by generating synthetic data for underrepresented groups, leading to fairer and more accurate models. It is important to carefully consider the potential biases in the original data and to apply augmentation techniques in a way that promotes fairness and equity. > Advanced data augmentation techniques, like GANs, can generate high-quality synthetic data that addresses bias by creating a more balanced representation of different groups. It is important to develop metrics that can accurately measure the impact of data augmentation on model performance and bias reduction. Future directions in data augmentation include the development of more sophisticated techniques that can automatically identify and address biases in datasets. By addressing these challenges, it is possible to further enhance the power of data augmentation in reducing bias and promoting more equitable and sustainable solutions. Meaning → Data Augmentation represents a suite of techniques employed to expand the volume and diversity of datasets by generating modified versions of existing data points.### Synthetic Data.
